text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: streaming p99 SLO breach in us-west-2. alerts: p99=2.1s (SLO=1.0s), p95=0.9s. Affected path: continuous-batching -> streaming fallback. Paging rate for KV cache spiked ~3x. Auto-remediation: none. Paging to on-call team.

alex: ack. I'm on it, joining bridge. page to sam (runtime) and tina (sre)

sam: got it. I'm seeing a correlated increase in batch sizes for streaming requests — scheduler is packing mixed-small sequences into large batches. KV cache eviction up, disk IO spikes on serving nodes.

tina: noticed a few customer 500s during the spike, but most errors are timeouts. Customers with streaming-heavy real-time flows hit p99 worst.

marco: leaderboard: top latency contributor is cont-batch scheduler + packer heuristics. Metrics: batch_size_mean up from 12 -> 48. seq_len distribution unchanged. suspect packing of short seqs into long batches causing stall for streaming consumers.

priya: can we split pools? route streaming connections to low-latency pool or cap max batch size for streaming route?

sam: yes — we have a runtime config flag: `max_batch_size` per route and `enable_streaming_priority`. Suggested hotfix: reduce `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 24 for streaming route and enable `streaming_priority=true` to preempt packer when streaming tokens arrive.

jess: what's the customer impact? any enterprise customers flagged?

tina: two customers on dedicated plans reported elevated latency (CS opened tickets). No data loss. Customer impact = elevated latency + some timeouts for long streaming. Recommend proactive notify if we don't fix in 60m.

alex: plan: 1) apply emergency config to streaming route on canary pool (10%) 2) monitor p99+ paging. 3) if good, roll to 100% in 10m. 4) follow-up postmortem.

sam: preparing canary patch now. patch payload:

```
route: streaming
  max_batch_size: 24
  streaming_priority: true
scheduler:
  fairness_weight: 1.2  # nudge to favor small seq
```

ops-bot: deploy started: canary streaming-config -> pool-usw2-canary (uid 8f3b)

marco: add defensive KV settings: lower `kv_max_entries` threshold to reduce eviction churn during high packer throughput (temp). I'll open a runtime ticket for rollback later.

ops-bot: canary deployed (8f3b). metrics: p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 1.05s within 90s on canary nodes. paging_iops down 40%.

tina: good signal. no customer errors on canary.

alex: proceed to roll to all streaming pools. rolling config to 5 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100 over 12min.

ops-bot: rollout 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% complete. final rollout id: r-2026-48921

sam: live note: we saw a transient bump at 50% as scheduler rebalanced, but p99 stabilized below 1.0s after the final step. We'll keep `streaming_priority` on for 24h.

priya: also suggest long-term: add explicit routing by seq_len: (<128 tokens) -> low-latency pool, >128 -> high-throughput. Plus packer fairness improvements.

marco: agreed. I'll file RFC for packer heuristics: dynamic cap based on recent seq_len histogram + tenant-weighted fairness.

jess: can we craft a short status blurb for CS to send to the two customers?

alex: draft: "We observed a temporary latency spike affecting streaming responses caused by an interaction between the continuous batching scheduler and short-sequence streaming traffic. We deployed a config change that reduces batch sizes for streaming and prioritizes streaming requests; metrics show p99 is back within SLO. No data loss. Root cause investigation and follow-up report will be shared by EOD." Please edit.

tina: lgtm. I'll post to status page and ping CS.

ops-bot: incident closed (4892103520). tags: contbatch, streaming, paging, hotfix. Follow-up: postmortem assigned to sam + marco, due in 72h.

alex: thanks team. next steps: 1) postmortem, 2) telemetry dashboard for `batch_size_by_route`, `paging_iops`, `p99_streaming`, 3) RFC for packer.

sam: saving logs + flame graphs to incident runbook: /incidents/4892103333/ (ops-bot attached)

priya: I'll add a short runbook step for oncall: if streaming p99 >1.5s then apply `max_batch_size:24` and enable `streaming_priority` on canary.

marco: note: we should consider automatic detection for mixed-seq packing anomalies (anomaly when mean batch_size / median_seq_len > threshold). filing ticket.

alex: closing thread here, but keep monitoring for 2h. :thumbsup:
